subject: North Ridge renewal: Q3 usage health + fallback plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@northridge.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: North Ridge renewal: Q3 usage health + fallback plan

Hi Elena —

Quick note ahead of our health sync: I attached a short usage report and the latency benchmarks we ran against your production traffic last quarter. High-level observations:

- Token spend: ~1.85B tokens in Q3 (prompt + generated). Month-over-month spike in May driven by a model retrain and a new A/B variant.
- Cost/ROI: Average inference cost per 1M tokens is down 12% after the batching and prefetch changes we rolled. Your reported customer value per 1M tokens continues to outpace costs; still room to optimize for embeddings-heavy workloads.
- Performance: 95th percentile latency for chat routes is ~180ms in eu-west when served on the current pinned variant; we saw a 40ms increase during the May spike.

Risk/ask: If North Ridge expects the new recommendation pipeline to be fully rolled by September, we recommend a staged commit increase and a canary runway to avoid throttling. Proposed immediate actions:

1) Lock a 10% headroom commit for Q4 (proposal attached).
2) Run a 2-week canary on Dedicated capacity with the quantized model variant.
3) Add an SLA addendum for burst capacity + fallback routing to a compatible smaller variant.

Attachments: usage_report_q3_northridge.pdf, latency_benchmarks.csv

Can you confirm whether procurement should be looped now? If useful, I can put together a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a DocuSign start-of-term addendum.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the summary and the quick look — the numbers align broadly with what our billing team has. A couple quick clarifications before we lock a MAP:

- The May spike was due to a monthly refresh job that sent a large batch of prompts; we expect similar occasional bursts once the recommender is live.
- Can you confirm the expected cost delta if we run the canary on Dedicated vs. staying hosted with burst?

Procurement (cc'd) prefers to see a draft of the proposed commit tiers and any language around service credits for latency regressions. If you can share those, I will route to legal and procurement for a fast review.

Also attaching our internal Q3 summary for context (separate file).

Best,

Markus / Karthik —

Saw Markus's note and Elena's reply. Quick internal alignment before we send a pricing MAP back to the customer:

- Recommended commit tiers (rounded):
  * Tier A (safe): 2.0B tokens / quarter (10% headroom) — baseline pricing + 8% discount.
  * Tier B (growth): 2.75B tokens / quarter — 15% discount, includes one scheduled canary (2 weeks) on Dedicated.
  * Burstable option: hourly burst credits for up to 30% additional throughput during promos.

- SLA addendum: propose a 99.9% availability target for pinned Dedicated with an automatic fallback to the quantized hosted variant. Credits for latency regressions (p95 > 250ms) can be structured as a partial monthly credit.

I prepared a short spreadsheet with pricing examples and run-rate impact (proposed_commit_options.xlsx). Karthik, please confirm the discount bands and whether we can include a limited one-time ramp credit in Q4 to help with the migration costs.

If we want to move fast, Markus should share the MAP + DocuSign link and ask procurement for a preferred review timeline.

Thanks —
